To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of CPSP following TTA is approximately 15%, that acute post-operative pain (APSP), as measured using a visual analog pain scale, is an independent predictor for CPSP following TKR, and that the odds for CPSP increase by approximately 50% for each unit of increase in APSP.
acute postoperative pain was a significant independent risk factor for chronic postsurgical pain at six months following total knee arthoplasty.

acute postoperative pain (APSP), as measured by the weighted mean pain scores (WMP) over 72 hours postoperative, was a risk factor for developing chronic postsurgical pain at 6 months (CPSP6) following total knee arthoplasty (TKA), even after adjusting for patient, surgical, and psychological confounding variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of acute and chronic pain in patients with osteoarthrosis of the knee joint after total knee arthroscopy.
the relationship between pain in the early postoperative period and the development of chronic pain in the medium term.
the development of chronic pain following total knee replacement surgery, a common procedure for knee osteoarthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute postoperative pain is a significant predictor of chronic pain after total knee arthroscopy, but that it is not the only factor.

acute postsurgical pain is a risk factor and independent predictor of chronic post surgical pain following total knee replacement at 6 months, even after adjusting for patient, surgical, and psychological confounding variables.
acute pain after surgery is a modifiable independent risk factor for the subsequent development of CPSP, and that the risk can be reduced through effective perioperative analgesia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acute pain is a modifiable factor in the development of chronic pain following total knee replacement.
acute postoperative pain is a risk factor of chronic postsurgical knee pain.
the acute pain after surgery can be a risk factor for developing chronic pain later on.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acute pain experience is important in the development of chronic pain.
acute pain is an important risk factor for chronic pain after TKA.
acute postoperative pain is a risk factor even after controlling for confounders.
